title: Train on what the model saw, and what one gradient step does to each turn
purpose: Recompute every turn's token log-probabilities on a GPU with the same model, on the context stored with the turn and on the full uncompacted history. Then, for one trajectory whose turn-level credit has both signs (a failed one if there is one), measure the first-order effect of one policy-gradient step on each turn, for trajectory-level and for turn-level advantages.

steps.display: lh.py trainer logprobs --trajectories <1 compacted + 1 not> --out credit/base/logprob-check.json
aws s3 cp s3://<bucket>/credit/base/logprob-check.json -   # one row per turn (first 12)
lh.py trainer update --trajectory base-t2-09-s0 --credit credit/base-c4/<it>.json --out credit/base/update-base-t2-09-s0.json
first-order change of each turn's mean token log-probability after one step (lr 1e-3)

checks.description: on the stored context, the trainer reproduces the rollout engine's log-probabilities (mean absolute difference below 0.05)
checks.because: Same weights, same chat template, same token ids; what is left is bf16 numerics of two engines.

checks.description: for compacted turns, the full history gives different log-probabilities: it is not what the model saw
checks.because: The prompt differs (longer, with observations the model never read), so every token's probability changes.

checks.description: with trajectory-level credit, every turn is pushed the same way, the bad decisions with the good ones (changes under 0.0001 count as none)
checks.because: Every turn has the same advantage, so the step moves the probability of good and bad decisions in the same direction.

checks.description: with turn-level credit, turns with a positive advantage go up and turns with a negative one go down
checks.because: The gradient of sum_t A_t log p_t moves each turn in the direction of its own advantage, to first order.

notes: 1 compacted turns checked; prompt lengths seen vs full: 1198/2005.
